P1 — complects label vocabulary (data) with heuristic acronym guessing (code); keep the lookup map as the source of truth
P1 — silent visible regression; don't replace a working lookup with a clever heuristic and call it equivalent
P1 — Liskov Substitution violation: strengthens preconditions, weakens postconditions; the typed CategoryId union was also dissolved
P1 — WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE; the explicit table made the algorithm trivial and correct, restore it as primary lookup
P1 — postcondition silently weakened; TESTED-NOT-PROVED with no tests in the diff; demands enumeration of f over known IDs vs prior table

issues.description: getCategoryLabel silently regresses known IDs: heuristic replaces the explicit CATEGORY_LABELS map without a regression test
issues.detail: The old adapter held an explicit map (e.g., 'trustboundaries' -> 'Trust Boundaries', 'forensics-ready' -> 'Forensics Ready', 'internet-exposed' -> 'Internet Exposed'). The new lib/categories.ts replaces it with a rule cascade: SPECIAL_CASES (empty) -> version regex -> length<=3 uppercase -> capitalize. 'trustboundaries' now renders 'Trustboundaries'. The invariant 'every previously known ID renders identically' is broken with no test asserting it. Liskov/Dijkstra frame this as a contract/postcondition weakening; Hickey/Pike frame it as data (vocabulary) hidden inside code (heuristic); Torvalds calls it a silent visible regression. Restore the explicit table as primary lookup; let the heuristic remain only as a fallback.

issues.description: Empty SPECIAL_CASES dictionary shipped as scaffolding with no entries
issues.detail: SPECIAL_CASES is exported as an empty Record with a comment promising future entries. Torvalds and Pike call this gratuitous abstraction / unearned abstraction; Hickey calls it speculation as code and an escape hatch the author already expects to need; Dijkstra calls it speculative infrastructure for a problem not yet known to exist. Either populate it now with the cases the old map covered (e.g., 'trustboundaries' -> 'Trust Boundaries') and use it as the primary lookup, or delete the empty container and add it when the first counter-example arrives.

issues.description: Module boundary for the Category vocabulary dissolved: typed CategoryId union and explicit CATEGORY_IDS removed
issues.detail: Previously the supported category set lived as a typed const CATEGORY_IDS with an exported CategoryId union, giving callers a checkable contract. The refactor leaves only a string-in/string-out function, so the abstract type 'Category' becomes 'any string the API sends.' Callers (CategorySelector, FindingsFilters, adapter) lose the typed vocabulary and there is no single place that states the supported categories and their canonical labels. Reintroduce a typed registry as the contract; treat the heuristic strictly as fallback.

issues.description: Heuristic 'length<=3 means acronym' is an unsound assumption about the future input domain
issues.detail: Rule 3 ('words of length <=3 are likely acronyms') happens to work for the current 14 IDs but commits the function to a strong claim about all future API category IDs ('new', 'old', 'all', 'log', 'web' would all be uppercased). Without an allow-list of known acronyms or a stated invariant 'API category IDs are guaranteed to be acronyms <=3 chars or capitalizable words,' the function is under-audited. Pair with regression test enumerating the legacy IDs.

issues.description: PR bundles three independent concerns (Risk Radar feature, ThreatScore rename, bar-chart refactor)
issues.detail: The diff conflates (a) the Risk Radar + category selector feature, (b) a wholesale 'Threat Score' -> 'Prowler ThreatScore' rename across unrelated files (risk-plot, threat-score component), and (c) a horizontal-bar-chart width/percentage computation refactor. Torvalds calls this three patches submitted as one and demands a split for bisectability. Hickey asks 'was this one decision or two?' — it reads as two — and notes that bundling complects review and revert. Split into independent commits per concern.

issues.description: selectedPoint state in risk-radar-view-client complects three concerns (highlighted dot, dropdown value, details-panel row)
issues.detail: A single piece of state (selectedPoint: RadarDataPoint) is used to mean the dot the user clicked on the radar, the value the dropdown shows, and the row whose severity breakdown is rendered. handleCategoryChange has to do data.find() to reconstruct what is really an id. Decompose: store selectedCategoryId: string | null as the single source of truth; derive selectedPoint via useMemo from data + id.

issues.description: CategorySelector encodes 'no selection' as the magic string 'all' inside the value space of category IDs
issues.detail: handleValueChange treats value === 'all' as the null/clear sentinel, but category IDs come from the API as arbitrary strings. If the API ever introduces a category with id 'all', the selector silently coerces to no-selection. Hickey calls it place-oriented signaling through a magic value with translations scattered at every boundary; Liskov calls it a classic abstraction leak mixing the sentinel into the value type. Use a separate UI state for 'no selection' or a non-collidable sentinel, and centralize the conversion.

issues.description: HorizontalBarChart bar width and displayed percentage use two different formulas that can disagree
issues.detail: calculatedWidth falls back to value/maxValue*100 (relative to the largest bar) while displayPercentage falls back to value/total*100 (share of total). When item.percentage is undefined, the rendered bar can be at 100% width while the label shows a much smaller percent, or vice versa. The invariant 'the rendered bar length matches the percentage shown next to it' is broken. Unify or document the divergence explicitly. Knuth notes that a literate comment stating 'width is scaled to the largest bar for legibility; the label is share-of-total' would also suffice if the divergence is intentional.

issues.description: HorizontalBarChart percentage fallback semantics silently changed from || to ?? — 0 no longer triggers fallback
issues.detail: calculatedWidth and displayPercentage now use (item.percentage ?? <fallback>). Nullish coalescing fires only on null/undefined; it does NOT fire on 0. Prior code used (item.percentage || ...), which fell back on 0. A legitimate item.percentage === 0 now renders width 0 and label 0%, where previously it would have fallen back to the computed ratio. State explicitly whether item.percentage === 0 is intended to display as 0% or trigger fallback.

issues.description: Filter-display layer now has two parallel mechanisms (DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES vs labelFormatter); category moved between them without unification
issues.detail: active-filter-badge.tsx drops the category__in entry while findings-filters.tsx passes labelFormatter and data-table-filter-custom.tsx applies it inside the multi-select item. Hickey notes the category label now lives in three places (API string, formatter, dropped badge entry) and that the dropdown will show formatted labels while the active-filter badge falls back to a generic path. Either keep both representations consistent (formatter applies to badge too) or commit to a single value->label function.

issues.description: SEVERITY_ORDER now has two keys mapping to the same ordinal 4 (Informational and Info) — injectivity invariant broken
issues.detail: Adding Info: 4 alongside Informational: 4 introduces a non-injective ordering map. Dijkstra calls this an unstated invariant violation: any consumer that reverse-maps ordinal to name or assumes ordinal uniqueness now sees ambiguity. Hickey/Pike/Liskov/Torvalds also flag it (at P2) as papering over an upstream inconsistency that should be normalized at the boundary. The correct discipline: pick one canonical key, normalize 'Info' -> 'Informational' on ingestion, keep the codomain injective.

issues.description: CategorySelector dead-but-defensive empty-string branch — control flow guarding an unreachable state
issues.detail: handleValueChange checks `value === '' || value === 'all'` but the SelectItem only ever emits 'all' or a category ID. The empty-string branch is unreachable. Dijkstra calls this DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE and demands proof of reachability or deletion; Knuth/Torvalds/Pike rate it P2 as dead code that should be removed or documented. Either prove '' is reachable (e.g., shadcn select emits '' on clear) and document the producer, or delete the branch.

issues.description: HorizontalBarChart computes Math.max(...data.map(d => d.value)) inside the .map callback — O(n^2)
issues.detail: maxValue is recomputed for every row instead of hoisted once above the map. n is small (~14 categories) so the perf cost is negligible, but the fix is free and makes the invariant 'maxValue is constant across rows' explicit. Dijkstra calls it 'evidence the author transcribed the fix rather than thinking about it'; Knuth marks it premature-optimization-but-trivial-fix; Hickey/Torvalds/Pike say lift it for readability and to avoid drift. Hoist maxValue (and total) above the .map.

issues.description: displayPercentage and calculatedWidth share fallback-chain shape but are not factored into one helper
issues.detail: Both expressions share the (item.percentage ?? derived) pattern with only minor differences (rounding, total vs maxValue). Knuth wants a literate comment explaining the two distinct quantities; Torvalds and Pike want a single helper `computePercentages(item, total, maxValue)` returning {width, display} to collapse the branching and prevent drift.

issues.description: DataTableFilterCustom passes formatted displayLabel into getBadgeLabel where a raw value was expected
issues.detail: Previously getBadgeLabel(entity, value) received the raw value; now it gets displayLabel (already formatted). If getBadgeLabel does any lookup/keying/comparison against entity fields, behavior changes silently for any filter that supplies a labelFormatter. Either rename the parameter and document it as presentational, or pass raw value here and formatted label separately to the renderer.

issues.description: Category filter badge removed from DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES with no commit-message explanation or visible replacement
issues.detail: The diff removes the 'category__in' entry from DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES but the findings page still exposes a Category filter. Torvalds wants the 'why' stated in the commit message; Liskov asks for confirmation that every supported filter still has a badge representation (otherwise applying the filter renders a generic fallback that no longer says 'Category').

issues.description: CustomDot 'isSelected' predicate compares against `payload.name || payload.category` — fragile equality on radar identity
issues.detail: currentCategory = payload.name || payload.category and the test is selectedPoint?.category === currentCategory. The predicate is correct only under the unstated precondition that selectedPoint.category equals whichever of name/category the radar library returns. The new isFaded flag amplifies the cost: every non-selected dot now visibly fades, so any identity mismatch produces a fully-faded chart with nothing highlighted. State the invariant on category identity, or key off categoryId which is already threaded through CategorySelector.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly on one P1: getCategoryLabel replaces an explicit ID->label map with a three-rule heuristic plus an empty SPECIAL_CASES dict, silently regressing at least one known ID ('trustboundaries' -> 'Trustboundaries' instead of 'Trust Boundaries') and dissolving the typed CategoryId vocabulary — all six reviewers flag this, framing it variously as a postcondition weakening (Liskov/Dijkstra), data hidden inside heuristic code (Hickey/Pike), an unaudited invariant (Knuth), or a clean visible regression (Torvalds). Five of six also call out SEVERITY_ORDER gaining a duplicate ordinal (Info: 4 alongside Informational: 4) as breaking the implicit injectivity invariant — Dijkstra rates it P1, the rest P2 — and want normalization at the boundary instead. The strongest preserved disagreement is on the HorizontalBarChart percentage refactor: Liskov and Dijkstra escalate it to P1 (the bar width and label can disagree because the two formulas diverge, AND the ?? swap means a legitimate 0 no longer triggers fallback), while Knuth/Torvalds/Pike treat it as P2 readability/perf nits. Torvalds and Hickey separately demand the PR be split — radar feature, ThreatScore rename, and bar-chart refactor are three independent concerns bundled into one diff. Recommend: restore an explicit, tested label table with heuristic as fallback only; normalize 'Info' at the boundary; unify the two percentage formulas (or document the intentional divergence); split the patch.
